- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot early in the forecast horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially after recent declines; model fails to account for mean reversion in bearish phases.
- Forecast tends to lag in downward trends — model often holds too much upward bias even as sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., multiple -0.28 values), reduce forecast by 5–10% relative to prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- In multi-day sentiment shifts (e.g., from +0.17 to -0.28), adjust forecast downward by 2–3 days before the sentiment reversal to capture turning point.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts when sentiment is mixed or trending downward — model often assumes continuation of prior trend.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model may overfit recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day high to prevent runaway spikes.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to recognize the “reversion to mean” — apply a 3–5 day lag correction for such cases.
